messages:
omar (Support): Creating warroom — ACME corp reporting repeated 5xx / 504 timeouts from hosted /v1/generate since ~10:12Z. Customer impact: API failures and streaming disconnects. Escalating to SRE.

jess (SRE): On it. Looking at gateway graphs — spike in upstream 502/504s and connection queue length at the edge. Correlating with auth-proxy 429s.

kai (Eng Runtime): saw a brief kv-cache miss storm at the same window, and a bunch of long-lived connections to the runtime pool. Could be overloaded connection pools + auth retries.

maria (Support): Customer says partial successes then long tails, some requests eventually succeed after retries. They are on enterprise plan, high throughput test during incident. Need an interim workaround for them.

jess (SRE): Mitigation actions in progress: 1) temporary increase ingress conn_pool size, 2) disable aggressive client-side retries for that customer via per-tenant quota, 3) kick auth-proxy canary back to previous. Executing now.

deploy-bot: deploy started by jess: rollback auth-proxy canary -> previous stable (deploy/hosted-auth-proxy)

jess (SRE): Command run:```kubectl -n hosted-prod rollout undo deploy/hosted-auth-proxy```
Confirming reduced 429s on auth-proxy, and edge conn queues dropping.

kai (Eng Runtime): I pushed a temporary kv-cache TTL increase and enabled extra accept threads on the runtime pool to reduce head-of-line blocking. Command:```rkctl runtime config set --pool-threads 64 --kv-cache-ttl 30s``` (will revert after postmortem).

ellie (Product): Customer comms: Maria, please send a status update acknowledging we see the failures, we've applied mitigations, and we'll follow up with RCA + ETA for permanent fix. Include regenerative workaround (reduce parallelism) so they can reduce failed requests.

maria (Support): On it, drafting message now. Will offer temporary rate-limit relaxation for their test token and note mitigations.

jess (SRE): Short-term status: auth-proxy 429s down to baseline, gateway 504 rate dropped ~85% in 15m, streaming disconnects reduced. Still seeing elevated latency for some long tails.

kai (Eng Runtime): Root cause hypothesis: auth proxy introduced a change in the canary that backpressured upstream token refresh endpoints; combination of heavy client concurrency and cold kv-cache misses amplified connection lifetimes and exhausted runtime conn pool.

ellie (Product): Action items (owners): - Postmortem doc + timeline (ellie) - Permanent auth-proxy fix + canary gating (jess + kai) - Improve per-tenant throttle rules & safe fallback (kai) - Customer follow-up + credit conversation (maria) - Add automated detection alert for auth-proxy 429 -> gateway 504 correlation (jess)

jess (SRE): I'll own the detection alert and the canary gating PR. Filing follow-up tasks.

kai (Eng Runtime): I'll take the runtime hardening and per-tenant fallback. Will open a PR to add circuit-breaker on long-lived runtime conns.

maria (Support): Customer update sent at 10:55Z. They acknowledged and asked for ETA for fix — said they're pausing heavy tests for now.

incident-bot: Incident created: INCIDENT-2026-03-17-ACME-504s, severity P2. War room archived after mitigations, follow-up tasks added.

ellie (Product): Let's schedule postmortem meeting tomorrow 10:00 PT. I'll create the doc and link all logs/graphs.

jess (SRE): Quick list of artifacts to include in postmortem: edge ingress graphs, auth-proxy traces, token refresh latency histogram, runtime conn pool metrics, kv-cache hit/miss timeline, and deploy history for yesterday's canary.

omar (Support): Thanks team. Keeping thread open for any new regressions or customer replies. :thumbsup:
